title: Code Reviewer Dispatcher operator routes, version 1
description: The routes of the Dispatcher that an operator or a deploy step calls with the operator credential (`Authorization: Bearer <DISPATCHER_OPERATOR_TOKEN>`, #730), next to `POST /probe` (probe-verdict.v1.json). No app credential opens them: an app must not be able to start canary VMs, which cost money. AppsCheckResponse is the answer of `POST /apps/check`: for each app the Dispatcher serves, whether its App could be reached with that app's credential and which features of the split it lacks. Ids, booleans and stable codes only: no URL, no credential, no text the App sent. 401 with the runner API's ErrorResponse, the same for every refusal, when the credential is missing or wrong. A reader ignores fields it does not know.

AppCheckCode.description: Why an app is not fine, from the Dispatcher's call to `GET /api/runners/v1/version` of that App with the app's dispatcher credential: `app_unreachable` (no answer), `app_rejected` (the App refused the credential or the request), `app_error` (the App failed, 5xx or 429), `app_too_old` (no version route, or features of the split are missing: see `missingFeatures`) or `app_answer_invalid` (an answer of another shape). Null: the App is reachable, takes the credential and has every feature the Dispatcher needs. The Dispatcher keeps the list in dispatcher/src/core/app-client.ts (`APP_FAILURES`); a test holds them equal.

AppCheck.description: The result for one app of the Dispatcher's registry.

id.description: The id of the app in the registry (`reviewer` for the legacy variables).

reachable.description: False only when no answer came.

credentialAccepted.description: True when the App took the credential, false when it refused it, null when that is not known (no answer, or an App that failed before it checked).

missingFeatures.description: The features of the split (`VersionResponse.features`) the App lacks; empty unless the code is `app_too_old` because of the answer.

AppsCheckResponse.description: The answer of `POST /apps/check`: 200 with every app, whatever each one's result (the caller reads the codes: a deploy step blocks on `app_unreachable` and `app_rejected`, not on `app_too_old`, because the live Apps are the previous release while a new one is rolled out). `ok` is true when every `code` is null.
